entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-j3rv-43j4-c7qm: jackson-databind has a PolymorphicTypeValidator bypass via generic type parameters that allows arbitrary class instantiation
entry.content:
jackson-databind has a PolymorphicTypeValidator bypass via generic type parameters that allows arbitrary class instantiation

Aliases: CVE-2026-54512

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind — fixed in 2.18.8
  • com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind — fixed in 3.1.4
  • com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind — fixed in 2.21.4
  • tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind — fixed in 3.1.4

`jackson-databind`'s `PolymorphicTypeValidator` (PTV) is the primary safety mechanism guarding polymorphic deserialization. When polymorphic typing is enabled and a type identifier contains generic parameters (i.e. the type ID string contains `<`), `DatabindContext._resolveAndValidateGeneric()` validates **only the raw container class name** (the substring before `<`) against the configured PTV. If the container type is approved, the method parses the full canonical type string via `TypeFactory.constructFromCanonical()` and returns the fully parameterized type **without ever validating the nested type arguments** against the PTV. The nested type arguments are then resolved, instantiated, and populated as beans during deserialization. An attacker who controls the type ID can therefore pla…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-hrmc-jmp7-mpm2: H2O.ai H2O vulnerable to deserialization attacks via a JDBC Connection URL
entry.content:
H2O.ai H2O vulnerable to deserialization attacks via a JDBC Connection URL

Aliases: CVE-2024-45758, PYSEC-2026-352

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • ai.h2o:h2o-core
  • h2o

H2O.ai H2O through 3.46.0.4 allows attackers to arbitrarily set the JDBC URL, leading to deserialization attacks, file reads, and command execution. Exploitation can occur when an attacker has access to post to the ImportSQLTable URI with a JSON document containing a connection_url property with any typical JDBC Connection URL attack payload such as one that uses queryInterceptors.

The vulnerability arises from improper handling of JDBC connection parameters, which can be exploited by bypassing regular expression checks and using double URL encoding. entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-wj3h-wx8g-x699: H2O has an External Control of File Name or Path vulnerability
entry.content:
H2O has an External Control of File Name or Path vulnerability

Aliases: CVE-2024-5986, PYSEC-2026-353

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • ai.h2o:h2o-core
  • h2o

A vulnerability in h2oai/h2o-3 version 3.46.0.1 allows remote attackers to write arbitrary data to any file on the server. This is achieved by exploiting the `/3/Parse` endpoint to inject attacker-controlled data as the header of an empty file, which is then exported using the `/3/Frames/framename/export` endpoint. The impact of this vulnerability includes the potential for remote code execution and complete access to the system running h2o-3, as attackers can overwrite critical files such as private SSH keys or script files.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-xqrx-qh46-34m7: snappy-java: JVM crash from unchecked ranges in Snappy.arrayCopy and SnappyOutputStream.rawWrite
entry.content:
snappy-java: JVM crash from unchecked ranges in Snappy.arrayCopy and SnappyOutputStream.rawWrite

Aliases: CVE-2026-116590

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • org.xerial.snappy:snappy-java — fixed in 1.1.10.9

### Impact `Snappy.arrayCopy(Object src, int offset, int byteLength, Object dest, int destOffset)` called a native `memcpy` without validating the ranges. A negative or oversized `byteLength` or offset read or wrote outside the arrays and crashed the JVM. `SnappyOutputStream.rawWrite` and `SnappyInputStream.rawRead`, and therefore the typed-array `write`/`read` methods, pass caller-supplied ranges to this method. ### Patches Fixed in 1.1.10.9 (#741). `Snappy.arrayCopy` checks both ranges before copying. The stream `read`/`write` methods validate offsets and lengths, and reject typed-array ranges whose byte size overflows `int`. ### Workarounds Validate offsets and lengths before calling these methods.

References:

  • https://github.com/xerial/snappy-java/security/advisories/GHSA-xqrx-qh46-34m7

snappy-java: Unbounded memory allocation from attacker-declared uncompressed lengtha

Aliases: CVE-2026-108106

Affected:

### Impact Several decompression paths in snappy-java allocate an output buffer sized by the uncompressed length declared in the first bytes of the compressed data, before decompressing or validating it. A few bytes of crafted input can therefore force an allocation of up to 2 GB, causing `OutOfMemoryError` (denial of service), or a `NegativeArraySizeException` for declared lengths of 2^31 or more. entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-gwq9-9ffj-mvrv: snappy-java: Heap buffer overflow in Snappy.uncompress*Array typed-array methods
entry.content:
snappy-java: Heap buffer overflow in Snappy.uncompress*Array typed-array methods

Aliases: CVE-2026-93451

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • org.xerial.snappy:snappy-java — fixed in 1.1.10.9

### Impact `Snappy.uncompressCharArray`, `uncompressShortArray`, `uncompressIntArray`, `uncompressLongArray`, `uncompressFloatArray` and `uncompressDoubleArray` sized the result array by dividing the declared uncompressed byte length by the element size, but native code wrote the full byte length. If the declared length is not a multiple of the element size, up to 7 bytes are written past the end of the Java array, corrupting the heap. ### Patches Fixed in 1.1.10.9 ([#739](https://github.com/xerial/snappy-java/pull/739)). These methods now reject uncompressed lengths that are not a multiple of the element size with `SnappyIOException`. ### Workarounds Check that `Snappy.uncompressedLength(input)` is a multiple of the element size before calling these methods.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-f63g-88cj-hjf9: IzPack has Path Traversal in UnpackerBase that allows writing files outside the installation directory via malicious pack entries
entry.content:
IzPack has Path Traversal in UnpackerBase that allows writing files outside the installation directory via malicious pack entries

Aliases: CVE-2026-54550

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:N/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • org.codehaus.izpack:izpack-installer — fixed in 5.2.7

### Summary IzPack's `UnpackerBase.unpack()` resolves pack-file target paths without any canonical-path or directory-containment check. An attacker who distributes a trojanized installer JAR (the format is unsigned) can include pack entries whose `targetPath` contains `../` sequences. entry.content:
Apache Log4j 1 to Log4j 2 bridge: silent log event loss in Log4j1XmlLayout due to unescaped XML 1.0 forbidden characters

Aliases: CVE-2026-34479

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:L/SA:N

Affected:

  • org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core — fixed in 2.25.4
  • org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core

The `Log4j1XmlLayout` from the Apache Log4j 1-to-Log4j 2 bridge fails to escape characters forbidden by the XML 1.0 standard, producing malformed XML output. Conforming XML parsers are required to reject documents containing such characters with a fatal error, which may cause downstream log processing systems to drop or fail to index affected records. Two groups of users are affected: * Those using `Log4j1XmlLayout` directly in a Log4j Core 2 configuration file. * Those using the Log4j 1 configuration compatibility layer with `org.apache.log4j.xml.XMLLayout` specified as the layout class. entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-794g-x443-36f7: Keycloak: Unauthorized access via improper validation of encrypted SAML assertions
entry.content:
Keycloak: Unauthorized access via improper validation of encrypted SAML assertions

Aliases: BIT-keycloak-2026-2092, CVE-2026-2092

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:L

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services
  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services
  • org.keycloak:keycloak-services — fixed in 26.5.5

Keycloak's SAML broker endpoint does not properly validate encrypted assertions when the overall SAML response is not signed. An attacker with a valid signed SAML assertion can exploit this by crafting a malicious SAML response, injecting an encrypted assertion for an arbitrary principal, leading to unauthorized access and potential information disclosure.
